alignments.note: Imperative; the ASV writes no ye beside it here.
Vocative construct noun with the supplied ye, rule 36; head on the noun.
Article on the rectum: the ASV writes no the for this phrase at all, rule 29.
Nomen rectum takes the relational of, headed on the noun, rule 19.
Conjunction to the written And, rule 14.
Article on a vocative takes only what the ASV writes for it, which here is nothing; the ye stays with the noun, rule 36.
Vocative noun with its supplied ye, rule 36.

Compound preposition rendered by the single word above fuses under rule 30, headed on the governing first morpheme under rule 23; the verbless clause's copula joins the prepositional predicate under rule 49, and the target head is the English preposition.
Article to the written the, rule 15.

review_notes: Two of the verse's three article morphemes go unrendered: the rectum's, because the ASV writes heavens of heavens with no the, and the vocative's, because rule 36 leaves the ye with the noun.

An alternative reading would head the fused preposition on the second morpheme as the one whose sense above carries; rule 23 settles it on the governing first morpheme, since neither carries content the other lacks.
